To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
DHEA is a glucocorticoid receptor antagonist, which may be used for prevention of the glucocorticoid-induced immune suppression in patients treated with glucocorticoids.

the immunoprotective effect of DHEA and DHEA(S) may be ascribed to their antiglucocortical action, that this effect is exerted at various levels, that it is not only DHEAS that acts in this way, and that the antiglucocorctical effect of DHEAS may be ascribed not only to the parent steroid but also to some of its metabolities, especially 7-hydroxy-DHEAS.
the immunoprotective effect of DHEA may be explained, at least partially, by its antiglucocortioid action at several levels of glucocorticoids action, including their synthesis, release and action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of DHEA in the light of the recent findings.
the question whether DHEA may be a promising agent in the treatment of some age-dependent diseases.
the mechanism of DHEA action and its metabolites, and the possibility of their application in the prevention of age-related degenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

DHEA and DHEAS are the most important natural antiglucocortioid hormones, the effects of which, however, are not limited to glucocorticoid receptors and the classical genomic mechanism of action of glucocorticoids.
DHEA and DHEAS may exert their beneficial effects in the organism through the action of DHEA and/or its 7-hydroylated metabolites as antiglucocortioids.
the effects of DHEAS are not only the result of its metabolism to androgens or estrogens, but that DHEA(S) itself, and its 7-hydoxylated derivatives may act at various levels as antiglucocorti-coids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DHEA is not "the youth hormone" in the sense that it may reverse aging, but it is an important hormone in the sense that its deficiency may be associated with some age-associated diseases.
DHEA(S) are not only precursors for biologically active androgenic and estrogens but that they may exert their own biological effects, which are of great importance in aging.
DHEA and DHEAS, as well as their hydroxylated derivatives may be considered as "the hormones of youth", which may be used as a tool in the prevention of aging-associated degenerative changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DHEA may be considered as a natural glucocorticoid antagonist and that its beneficial effects may be ascribed to this feature.

DHEA may be considered as a natural immunomodulatory steroid, which may be used as a tool in therapy of immunodepressed patients, especially those suffering from the consequences of glucocorticoids therapy, as well as of the immunosuppressive effects of aging.

it is necessary to study not only the effects of DHEAS but also of its 7-hyroxylated metabolites, especially 7-hydroxy-DHEA and 7-hydro-xy-DHEAS, in the context of the mechanism of glucocoicoid action.
